notes: Input for build/New-CrosswalkSeed.ps1 (hand-maintained). Control IDs are public identifiers; every paraphrase is VSAT-written (12 words or fewer). No standards text is embedded. Imported frameworks (DISA STIG, licensed CIS reviews) come from build/crosswalk/imported/.

frameworks.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
frameworks.note: Rows are proposed by VSAT rule category (build/New-CrosswalkSeed.ps1); a reviewer confirms them before they count as verified.

controls.paraphrase: Manage system accounts through their whole life cycle.
Enforce approved authorizations for access to resources.
Control how information flows within and between systems.
Separate duties so no single person holds conflicting privileges.
Grant only the privileges each user or process needs.
Limit consecutive failed logons and lock or delay afterwards.
Limit concurrent sessions per account or console.
Lock idle sessions after a period of inactivity.
End sessions automatically after defined conditions.
Authorize and protect remote access to systems.
Provide enough storage for audit logs.
Review and analyze audit records for suspicious activity.
Use synchronized, reliable time stamps in audit records.
Protect audit information and tools from unauthorized change.
Retain audit records long enough for investigations.
Generate audit records for defined events.
Set and enforce secure configuration settings.
Provide only essential functions, ports, protocols and services.
Keep an accurate inventory of system components.
Back up system and user data and protect the backups.
Recover and reconstitute the system to a known state.
Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users.
Identify and authenticate devices before connecting them.
Manage authenticators such as passwords, keys and certificates.
Scan for and remediate known vulnerabilities.
Replace or justify components no longer vendor supported.
Prevent information leaking through shared system resources.
Protect resource availability through allocation and priority.
Monitor and control communications at system boundaries.
Protect confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information.
Terminate network connections after inactivity.
Establish and manage cryptographic keys.
Issue and manage public key certificates properly.
Protect information at rest.
Partition the system into separate physical or logical domains.
Keep a separate execution domain for each process.
Identify, report and correct system flaws promptly.
Monitor the system to detect attacks and anomalies.
Detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware and information.
Manage and retain information according to requirements.

frameworks.name: IEC 62443-3-3 system requirements
frameworks.note: SR identifiers with VSAT-written paraphrases only; no IEC text. Rows are proposed by rule category until an OT reviewer confirms them.

controls.paraphrase: Identify and authenticate every human user.
Identify and authenticate software processes and devices.
Manage accounts: add, change, disable and remove.
Manage authenticators such as passwords and keys.
Enforce strong password-based authentication.
Operate public key infrastructure certificates correctly.
Limit unsuccessful login attempts.
Control access arriving over untrusted networks.
Enforce authorization for every user action.
Lock sessions after inactivity.
Terminate remote sessions automatically.
Limit concurrent sessions.
Record security-relevant events in audit records.
Provide sufficient audit storage capacity.
Time-stamp audit records from a synchronized source.
Protect the integrity of transmitted information.
Detect unauthorized changes to software and information.
Protect audit information from unauthorized access.
Protect confidentiality of information at rest and in transit.
Use recognized cryptography and manage keys.
Segment control system networks from other networks.
Monitor and control traffic at zone boundaries.
Partition data and applications by criticality.
Give authorized people read access to audit logs.
Monitor the control system continuously for security events.
Keep operating during denial-of-service conditions.
Manage resources to prevent exhaustion.
Back up control system information.
Recover and reconstitute to a known secure state.
Configure network and security settings to a baseline.
Disable unnecessary functions, ports, protocols and services.
Maintain an inventory of control system components.

frameworks.name: MITRE ATT&CK Mitigations
frameworks.note: From each rule's attack.mitigation field, checked against the pinned ATT&CK catalog (data/attack). Names shown come from that catalog.
